title: Handle plain Step Functions execution errors
body:
`StepFunctionGetExecutionOutputOperator` raises `JSONDecodeError` when `DescribeExecution` returns an ordinary error such as `States.TaskFailed`. AWS documents [`error` as a string](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/step-functions/latest/apireference/API_DescribeExecution.html#API_DescribeExecution_ResponseSyntax), whereas `output` contains JSON data.

Return non-JSON errors unchanged, including empty strings. Preserve JSON-decoded error return values for compatibility and keep invalid success output and service exceptions visible. Document that fetching an error may complete the Airflow task successfully; checking remote execution success remains the responsibility of `StepFunctionExecutionSensor`. The documentation also explains the constraints on string results with `multiple_outputs` and dynamic task mapping.

Validation on upstream `5799660c4d41e95b8c3ce836bd9003c3e4f3a998`, Python 3.10 in the official Linux/amd64 Breeze CI image:

- Related Step Functions operator, hook, sensor and trigger tests: 38 passed with two workers after the rebase and review changes. The new client-backed regression explicitly closes its boto3 client.
- Initial before/after regression: 4 failures against the unchanged operator; all related tests pass with the fix. SDK responses use botocore Stubber, not live AWS.
- Regular/manual prek, provider mypy, commit-message checks and `git diff --check` passed. Selective-check was run against the complete PR diff.
- The wider dependent-provider and Airflow-version matrices, documentation build, live AWS and full task-runner/XCom integration were not run locally.

@@ -59,6 +59,17 @@ Get an AWS Step Functions execution output
 To fetch the output from an AWS Step Function state machine execution you can
 use :class:`~airflow.providers.amazon.aws.operators.step_function.StepFunctionGetExecutionOutputOperator`.
 
+The operator decodes JSON execution output. When the execution has an error instead,
+it returns the error string unchanged if it is not valid JSON. JSON-formatted errors
+continue to be decoded to their corresponding Python values.
+
+Fetching an error does not by itself fail the Airflow task. This operator does not wait
+for completion or check that the execution succeeded; use
+:class:`~airflow.providers.amazon.aws.sensors.step_function.StepFunctionExecutionSensor`
+to check the execution state. A returned error string is not suitable for
+``multiple_outputs=True`` or downstream dynamic task mapping, which require a mapping
+or a mappable collection, respectively.
+
 .. exampleinclude:: /../../amazon/tests/system/amazon/aws/example_step_functions.py
     :language: python
     :dedent: 4

@@ -199,7 +199,10 @@ def execute(self, context: Context):
         if "output" in execution_status:
             response = json.loads(execution_status["output"])
         elif "error" in execution_status:
-            response = json.loads(execution_status["error"])
+            try:
+                response = json.loads(execution_status["error"])
+            except json.JSONDecodeError:
+                response = execution_status["error"]
 
         self.log.info("Got State Machine Execution output for %s", self.execution_arn)

+    @pytest.mark.parametrize(
+        ("error", "expected_output"),
+        [
+            pytest.param("States.TaskFailed", "States.TaskFailed", id="plain_error"),
+            pytest.param("", "", id="empty_error"),
+            pytest.param("오류", "오류", id="unicode_error"),
+            pytest.param("{message", "{message", id="non_json_error"),
+            pytest.param('{"message": "failed"}', {"message": "failed"}, id="json_object_error"),
+            pytest.param('"failed"', "failed", id="json_string_error"),
+            pytest.param("42", 42, id="json_number_error"),
+            pytest.param("null", None, id="json_null_error"),
+        ],
+    )
+    def test_execute_describe_execution_error(self, error, expected_output):
+        client = boto3.client(
+            "stepfunctions",
+            region_name="us-east-1",
+            aws_access_key_id="testing",
+            aws_secret_access_key="testing",
+        )
+        op = StepFunctionGetExecutionOutputOperator(
+            task_id=self.TASK_ID, execution_arn=EXECUTION_ARN, aws_conn_id=None, region_name="us-east-1"
+        )
+        with closing(client), Stubber(client) as stubber, mock.patch.object(op.hook, "conn", client):
+            stubber.add_response(
+                "describe_execution",
+                {
+                    "executionArn": EXECUTION_ARN,
+                    "stateMachineArn": STATE_MACHINE_ARN,
+                    "startDate": datetime(2026, 1, 1, tzinfo=timezone.utc),
+                    "status": "FAILED",
+                    "error": error,
+                },
+                {"executionArn": EXECUTION_ARN},
+            )
+            assert op.execute({}) == expected_output
+            stubber.assert_no_pending_responses()
+
+    @mock.patch.object(StepFunctionGetExecutionOutputOperator, "hook", spec=StepFunctionHook)
+    def test_execute_rejects_invalid_json_output(self, mocked_hook):
+        mocked_hook.describe_execution.return_value = {"output": "not-json"}
+        op = StepFunctionGetExecutionOutputOperator(task_id=self.TASK_ID, execution_arn=EXECUTION_ARN)
+        with pytest.raises(json.JSONDecodeError):
+            op.execute({})
